metadata.subject: Data Structures
metadata.title: Discover Arrays
metadata.description: Use numbered indexes to access and replace values in fixed positions.

learning_objectives: Read a value at a numbered index.
Explain that an array position stays fixed.
Update selected positions to reach a target array.

mission.title: Use the indexes
mission.description: Watch how each numbered position identifies exactly one value.

introduction.title: An array is an ordered row of positions
introduction.content: Every item has an index: a small number that tells you exactly where it lives.
points: Reading an index does not move any values.
Replacing one index does not change the others.

worked_example.title: Read and replace
worked_example.content: Use the index first, then act on the value at that fixed position.

steps.explanation: Index 2 contains 10 because counting begins at 0.
Only position 3 changes; every other index stays in place.

worked_example.conclusion: An index is an address for one exact array position.

next.title: Now you try.
next.content: Follow the indexed operations in the array below.

next-step: Index 1 tells us to look at the second cell.
Updating an index changes only that one fixed position.
Reading an index returns the value currently stored there.

prediction.heading: Before the update…
prediction.question: What value will the next update write into the array?
prediction.selection_message: Your prediction: {prediction}. Now run the update.
prediction.pending_message: Make a prediction before the next array operation.
prediction.required_message: Choose the value you think will be written next.

result.actual: The next update writes {actual} into its fixed position.

actions.label: Read an indexed value
actions.task: Click the requested index to read its value.

actions.label: Replace one position
actions.task: Click the requested index and enter its replacement value.

actions.label: Read the updated position
actions.task: Click the updated index and read the value now stored there.

challenge.title: Array challenge
challenge.start_message: Transform the array by applying the displayed indexed updates.
challenge.continue_message: Challenge complete. Keep experimenting with fixed positions.

phases.title: Reach the target array
phases.instruction: Apply each indexed update until YOUR ARRAY matches the target.
phases.feedback: Compare every numbered position with the target array.

guidance.start_message: Use the indexes to make the requested changes.

items.content: An update only changes the cell with the matching index.

phases.title: Update two positions
phases.instruction: Reach TARGET using the numbered updates.
phases.feedback: Use the index named by the next operation.

guidance.start_message: Use the target to reason about which fixed positions will change.

phases.title: Transform an unfamiliar array
phases.feedback: An index names a position, not a value.

constraints.operation_limit_message: All three operations were used before the target was reached.

guidance.start_message: Plan the fixed-position updates before using your three operations.

phases.title: Solve with three operations
phases.instruction: Reach TARGET while keeping each update at its intended index.
phases.feedback: Compare each index before applying the next operation.

guidance.start_message: Work from the target state with no hints.

phases.title: Master indexed updates
phases.instruction: Apply the unfamiliar index changes independently.
phases.feedback: Keep your attention on positions, not on where a value appears.

thinking.title: Simulate indexed operations
thinking.instruction: Do not change the array yet. Apply every indexed operation in your head.
thinking.do_not_execute: Do not perform these operations in the playground. Work through them mentally.

prediction_fields.label: Final array
prediction_fields.prompt: What will the final array contain?

prediction_fields.label: Read value
prediction_fields.prompt: What value does the READ operation return?

feedback.all_correct: You tracked every fixed position correctly.
feedback.incorrect: Reapply each SET only at its numbered index.

solve.title: Expert Arrays
solve.instruction: Apply the unfamiliar indexed operations with no hints.
solve.operation_rule: Each read or update counts once.
solve.perfect_result: You completed the exact indexed plan.

quiz.question: What does index 0 identify in an array?

discovery.title: Array discovery
discovery.summary: An array uses indexes as stable addresses, so you can read or replace one exact position.

sections.title: What?
sections.content: An array stores an ordered row of values, each with an index.

sections.title: Why?
sections.content: A fixed index makes direct access and replacement predictable.

alternate_explanations.title: Think of lockers
alternate_explanations.content: An index is like a locker number: it tells you exactly where one item belongs.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, why does changing one array index leave the other positions unchanged?
recall.model_answer: Each index refers to one fixed position, so an update replaces only the value stored at that position.
